[[Houston Rockets]] (1991) |awards = }} '''Jerome McKinley "Gerald" Henderson''' (born [[January 16]] [[1956]]) is a retired [[United States|American]] [[basketball]] player. He was a [[shooting guard]] who had a 13-year career in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] from 1979 until 1992. He played for the [[Boston Celtics]], [[Seattle SuperSonics]], [[New York Knicks]], [[Philadelphia 76ers]], [[Milwaukee Bucks]], [[Detroit Pistons]], and [[Houston Rockets]]. Henderson was born in [[Richmond, Virginia]]{{cite web|title=''Gerald Henderson (II)''|work=Imdb.com|url=http://www.imdb.com/name/nm1484911/bio|accessdate=2007-03-21}} and attended [[Virginia Commonwealth University]]. He was most famous for his steal of a [[James Worthy]] pass to score a game-tying layup in game two of the [[1984 NBA Finals]] between the Boston Celtics and the [[Los Angeles Lakers|L.A. Lakers]]. The Celtics eventually prevailed in overtime. As of 2006, he and his wife run a real estate business in [[Blue Bell, Pennsylvania]]. Gerald is currently an analyst on the 76ers post game live. Their son, [[Gerald Henderson, Jr.]] attends [[Duke University]], where he has played three years as a member of the Duke basketball team. He fills the athletic swingman role that has been missing since the 2003-2004 season ended.[http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=22724&SPID=1845&DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=941766 Coach K Has Big Plans For The Summer - GoDuke.com—Official Athletics Web site of Duke University] On April 20th, WRAL reported that Gerald Henderson Jr. will enter the NBA draft, but it is unknown if he will hire an agent.
